english_verification.review_scope: Checked H83 ruler and rival Tag, the English names of H73 and I14, English national-idea names/text and representative scripted effects, and claims actually present in the retrieved English Wiki chunk; not a full source-code audit.
unresolved: The checked English Wiki page is an infobox-only entry and does not corroborate the source article's account of the 894 entry into the Middle Serpentspine or the subsequent eastward exile of heretics.
The Wiki page does not establish mission mechanics, Dreamfire gain conditions, purge effects, value scores, or current implementation; those claims are not attributed to Wiki verification.

rationale.colonization: Late game requires handling underground empty provinces and population resets.
rationale.complexity: Resources, underground holds, and purge progress are interdependent.
rationale.dark_story: Explicitly makes the purging and extermination of a sapient people state policy.
rationale.difficulty: Players report long late-game waits for purging; this has not been tested in-game.
rationale.diplomacy: The crusade route is scarcely centered on cooperation.
rationale.early_pressure: The exiled starting position and feud with the former kin create pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Dreamfire, prophecy, and dream-forging are central to the state.
rationale.narrative_density: The exile, prophecy, hegemony, and crusade phases are clearly defined.
rationale.tall_play: Hold-forging matters, but the main loop is offensive.
rationale.trade_economy: Minerals and looting sustain the country.
rationale.warfare: Dreamfire directly encourages war against the Dwarves.

identity.appearance: An Old Dookan Black Orc exile warband led by Zog in 1444.
identity.formation_scope: Within H83, the warband becomes a dream hegemon and adopts the Dreamfire Crusade reform; the Tag does not change.
predecessors: Gor Vazumbrog exiles (a worldbuilding predecessor, not a prerequisite Tag).

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. Multiple candidate sets and conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneously stacked; whether new ideas are adopted on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: When Zog Shadowdreamer was exiled and driven out of Gor Vazumbrog by the Skewered Drake it was for his heretic vision: In a strange prophetic dream he saw the world from the eyes of Dookan himself. Banished for heresy, he left with other believers in his Dream, the Great Dream, or Kabir Drahm in Orcish. It now serves as the unifying cause for Zog's warband as they find their way to the place revealed to him in the dream: The abandoned hold of Gor Ozumbrog.

description.text: With our Dream leading us ever closer to Gor Ozumbrog, we need to prepare the surrounding caves and caverns for our new country. To that end we will need to settle every nook and cranny, every last spot up to the hold of our desire.

description.text: The Sagah, the Shadow Soldiers of Shadowdreamer are a fearsome unit. Clad in black fabric with the symbol of the Dream, a closed eye behind a clenched fist on their back, they hide in the dark caverns. There they wait so that they can surprise their enemy suddenly without warning. With the Sagah supporting us, the shadows are no longer merely hiding places. Instead, the shadows can be turned into potential traps waiting eagerly to be sprung.

description.text: The Drahmgrall are the Dream-Speakers of Shadowdreamer. These leading shamans are those that receive the visions coaxed forth by sleep that the orcs of Shadowdreamer depend on for spiritual guidance. They traverse the dreamscape where they see through Dookan's eyes and witness strange and otherworldly vistas: Frozen forests beneath rivers of molten rock, swords shattering on dangling cave moss, inexplicable lights dancing deep within the dark.

description.text: Only through their faith in the Dream could the warband stay together during the exile from Gor Vazumbrog, animated by the purpose laid out for them in Dookan's Dream. This purpose urges them ever forward towards fulfilling the Dream, labouring towards the goal that not even the Drahmgrall can fathom for now. Still, their devotion keeps them going, united by faith.

description.text: The Order of the Farun Chashm are reclusive shamans and sages living as hermits on the borders of Shadowdreamer who meditate on matters of state and innovation. This order of recluses see themselves as the opposite face of the Kabir Drahm from the Drahmgrall, calling themselves the "Forgotten Eye" Rumours spread that the strictness of their adherence to the Dream is a matter of debate. In exchange for being left mostly to their own machinations, they offer their services to the government as occasional advisors by bringing in new ideas from beyond the country. Their less zealous demeanour also makes them more agreeable merchants and diplomats, where they can gather foreign knowledge and bring it back to their home.

description.text: Before Shadowdreamer there was the Segbandal, an alliance of five dwarven holds. There, the dwarves had to share among themselves, exchanging goods and manpower. We have no need for that, we can use everything we produce ourselves. In the name of Dookan we claim these riches for ourselves, and only ourselves now. We will usurp the dwarven machinery's original purpose and bend them to our will. Mines, farmsteads, quarries, workshops, they will all serve Dookan.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players unwilling to engage with an ethnic-purge theme or unable to tolerate late-game waits for population processing.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First establish a mountain base through raids; in the mid-game, use Dreamfire to drive conquest; late game brings a crusade alongside purging and colonization management.
player_overview.overview: Shadowdreamer is a Black Orc exile warband led by Zog, driven out of Gor Vazumbrog by the Skewered Drake. You seize holds along underground passages, build Dreamfire, forge resources, and organize special troops; the country then becomes a dream hegemon and ultimately enters a crusade against the Dwarves. Its defining feature is that warfare and population purges directly feed the national mechanic. The cost is not only late-game waiting for purges and colonization, but also a story arc that explicitly moves toward systematic genocide.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy dark fantasy, Orcish underground conquest, and a strong resource loop.
signature_features: Dreamfire accumulates through fighting Dwarves, destroying holds, and purging populations.
The exile warband transforms into a dream hegemon and Dreamfire Crusade within the same country.
Underground holds, dream-forging, and special troops create a highly aggressive loop.
player_overview.tagline: Lead exiled Black Orcs to conquer the Serpentspine through Dreamfire and prophecy, and follow the path to a Dreamfire Crusade.

reasons: The Dreamfire mechanic is tightly tied to campaign objectives.
A dark national transformation driven by exile and prophecy.
Distinctive underground warfare and special troops.
warnings: Late-game waits for purging may disrupt the pace.
The central narrative concerns systematic genocide against the Dwarves.

positive_indicators: The exiled warband's early phase includes a survival motive, but this does not offset the later genocidal policy.
values.rationale: Current mechanics turn the purging of Dwarven populations and destruction of holds into Dreamfire income, while the casus belli and reform text openly advocate eliminating Dwarves. The score concerns institutionalized genocide, not Orcish identity or ordinary warfare.
red_flags: Gaining Dreamfire by purging Dwarven populations.
Treating the extermination of Dwarves as a justified war aim.
National institutions continually encourage hold destruction and population removal.
